paper.title: Multiparametric MRI radiomics and clinical features for preoperative prediction of high-grade meningioma: a two-centre retrospective study.
paper.abstract:
Background: Preoperative identification of high-grade meningioma remains challenging using clinical and conventional imaging features. We compared MRI radiomic and clinical models and assessed whether their integration improved external discrimination.
Materials And Methods: This retrospective two-centre study included 284 patients, with 227 used for training and 57 for independent external testing. Radiomics from contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI), T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) underwent training-cohort screening, correlation filtering, and LASSO selection. The primary comparison assessed external area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for joint-clinical versus clinical logistic regression (LR) models. Secondary comparisons assessed adding clinical predictors to joint imaging and combining sequences relative to T2WI. Bootstrap-based normal-approximation comparisons with paired resampling and Holm correction evaluated these three contrasts. Calibration, decision curves, and K-nearest neighbour (KNN) models were exploratory.
Results: The external cohort contained 48 low-grade and 9 high-grade tumours. All four imaging-only LR models had higher external bootstrap-mean AUC point estimates than the clinical model (0.663; 95% CI, 0.467-0.840). CE-T1WI yielded 0.863 (0.755-0.949), and FLAIR yielded 0.838 (0.724-0.932). T2WI and joint imaging yielded 0.719 (0.555-0.862) and 0.807 (0.640-0.941), respectively. The joint-clinical model had an external AUC of 0.754 (0.557-0.920). Imaging-only Brier scores (0.113-0.127) were lower than those of clinical (0.246) and joint-clinical (0.209) models. Both clinical and joint-clinical predictions overestimated risk in the external cohort. The primary joint-clinical versus clinical bootstrap-mean AUC difference was 0.091 (95% CI, -0.126 to 0.309; Holm-adjusted P = 0.410). None of the three planned contrasts remained significant after Holm correction.
Conclusion: MRI radiomics showed promising external discrimination and lower probability error than the clinical model in this cohort. These findings support further evaluation of radiomics for preoperative grade prediction, while the incremental benefit of clinical-radiomic integration remains unconfirmed.

paper.title: Development and external validation of age-specific predictive models for sepsis in critically ill neonates and children using multidimensional hematological parameters: a multicenter retrospective study.
paper.abstract:
Background: Sepsis remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in neonatal and pediatric intensive care units (NICU/PICU). Given the rapid clinical deterioration of these vulnerable populations, shifting from reactive diagnosis to proactive prediction of sepsis onset is crucial. Multidimensional hematological parameters may provide new insights for risk stratification. While routine complete blood count (CBC) is widely used, the predictive potential of high-dimensional hematological cell morphology features that extend beyond traditional CBC remains under-investigated in large-scale pediatric cohorts.
Methods: This multicenter study utilized a large-scale dataset from the CALM2302 project, encompassing 17,066 critically ill neonates and children across 30 Chinese hospitals between October 2020 and October 2023. We developed population-specific CatBoost models for NICU and PICU to predict sepsis onset. To mitigate class imbalance, random undersampling was applied to the training sets. From a candidate pool of 1,924 parameters (37 routine CBC and 1,887 research features), optimized signatures of approximately 200 features were selected for each population. Model performance was evaluated by the area under the ROC curve (AUC) across internal and dual external validation cohorts. Furthermore, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis was performed to ensure model interpretability and identify key biological predictors.
Results: Among the total cohort, 10,347 infants were categorized into the NICU cohort (sepsis incidence: 7.48%), while 6,719 children formed the PICU cohort (sepsis incidence: 10.92%). CatBoost was identified as the optimal architecture after benchmarking nine machine learning algorithms. The population-specific simplified 18-variable models demonstrated robust performance. In the NICU cohort, the model achieved an internal AUC of 0.846 and external AUCs of 0.742 and 0.827. For the PICU cohort, corresponding AUCs were 0.803, 0.717, and 0.811. These simplified models maintained highly comparable discriminative power to the full models (range of AUC attenuation: 0.005-0.027). SHAP analysis identified 18 key predictive features for each cohort, with only two shared features between the two populations and the remaining being cohort-specific. Notably, most of these 18 features were research parameters rather than traditional blood counts indices. Furthermore, most of these features remained statistically significant in multivariable analyses after adjustment for age, sex, and study sites.
Conclusions: In this large multicenter cohort, we developed and validated simplified 18-variable models that accurately predict sepsis in both neonatal and pediatric populations. By capturing early hematological morphological alterations beyond traditional blood counts, these models offer a robust, interpretable, and clinically accessible solution for proactive sepsis management in intensive care units.

paper.title: Automated CT segmentation of diffuse pseudomyxoma peritonei lesions using a hybrid deep learning model.
paper.abstract:
Purpose: To develop and externally validate DATUnet-a hybrid deep learning framework integrating DenseBlock encoding, atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP), and a lightweight Transformer bottleneck-for automated segmentation of diffuse pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP) lesions on contrast-enhanced CT.
Materials And Methods: This retrospective, dual-centre study enrolled 71 patients (59 primary centre, 12 external centre). Primary centre cases were allocated to training (n = 46, 6-fold cross-validation), independent held-out test (n = 7), and internal prospective validation (n = 6) cohorts; 12 external cases formed an independent external validation cohort. Lesions were independently annotated by two senior radiologists using intraoperative records as reference. DATUnet was evaluated using DSC, IoU, HD95, precision, and recall, and benchmarked against SwinUNet and nnUNetv2 under identical conditions. Model interpretability was assessed with Grad-CAM.
Results: On the independent test set, DATUnet achieved DSC 92.7%, IoU 87.2%, and HD95 24.098 mm. Internal prospective validation yielded DSC 92.4% and HD95 20.192 mm; external validation yielded DSC 84.9% and HD95 24.901 mm, confirming preserved generalization across institutions, scanners, and bowel-preparation protocols. DATUnet outperformed SwinUNet (DSC 81.3%) and nnUNetv2 (DSC 55.3%) across all overlap and boundary metrics. Grad-CAM visualizations demonstrated strong spatial correspondence between model attention and radiologist-annotated mucinous deposits, including regions with infiltrative growth patterns.
Conclusion: DATUnet achieves robust, reproducible automated segmentation of diffuse PMP lesions across diverse imaging environments, offering a quantitative foundation for preoperative lesion mapping, anatomical characterization, and cytoreductive surgery decision-making in clinical practice.

paper.title: Fully Automated Segmentation of Chronic Total Occlusion Lesions on Coronary CT Angiography Using Deep Learning.
paper.abstract: Reliable quantitative assessment for chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesions depends on accurate segmentation of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) images. However, incomplete contrast opacification and complex lesion morphology make precise delineation particularly challenging. We developed an Atrous Attention U-Net (AAU-Net) for CTO segmentation and integrated it into a fully automated workflow comprising heart localization, CTO localization, and lesion segmentation. This retrospective study included 565 CTO lesions from 551 patients who underwent prospectively ECG-gated CCTA at three centers. Standalone segmentation used reference-mask-derived lesion-containing slices and regions of interest, whereas the automated workflow used predicted localization without reference-mask information or manual correction. Under reference-defined localization, AAU-Net achieved a Dice score of 0.8421 and intersection over union of 0.7312 in the internal test set, although performance varied by anatomical location and center. Performance decreased in the fully automated workflow, with Dice scores of 0.6922 in the internal test set, 0.5822 in external test set 1, and 0.6480 in external test set 2, potentially reflecting localization errors and differences between the separately trained segmentation models. In an exploratory locked-model radiomics analysis, features derived from automated segmentations showed numerically lower predictive performance than those derived from manual segmentations. Overall, AAU-Net showed favorable segmentation performance under reference-defined localization, but the fully automated workflow demonstrated lower performance that varied across centers. The radiomics findings demonstrate technical feasibility rather than established clinical utility. Further optimization and larger prospective multicenter validation are required before clinical deployment.

paper.title: Multichannel Deep Learning Radiomics for Predicting Chemoimmunotherapy Response in Gastric Cancer: Multicenter Validation and Chemotherapy-alone Specificity Assessment.
paper.abstract:
Rationale And Objectives: To develop and validate a computed tomography-based model integrating multichannel deep learning and radiomics for predicting pathologic significant response (PSR) to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NACI) in locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC), and to assess whether the model specifically captures immunotherapy-related phenotypes by testing it on a chemotherapy-alone cohort.
Materials And Methods: This multicenter study included 455 patients with LAGC: 411 receiving NACI (split into training, internal validation, and external test set 1) and 44 receiving chemotherapy alone (test set 2). From three-dimensional (3D) segmentations, the largest axial, coronal, and sagittal slices were stacked as three-channel input for a pretrained ResNet50 to extract deep features; radiomic features were extracted from the 3D volume. Features were fused, reduced by the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator, and modeled with a support vector machine to construct a deep learning radiomics (DLR) signature. A combined model further incorporated mismatch repair status, programmed death-ligand 1 combined positive score, and tumor grade. Model performance was evaluated by area under the curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis, with SHAP for interpretability.
Results: The multichannel model outperformed single-plane models (AUCs: 0.783, 0.749, 0.706). The DLR model achieved the highest AUCs (0.827, 0.802, 0.776), surpassing radiomics-only (0.756, 0.712, 0.691) and multichannel deep models. Critically, its AUC dropped to 0.597 in the chemotherapy-alone cohort. SHAP provided global and individual feature attributions.
Conclusion: The multichannel DLR model accurately predicts PSR to NACI in LAGC. The substantial performance decline in the chemotherapy-alone cohort suggests that the captured imaging phenotypes may be more closely associated with immunotherapy-related response, rather than with general chemosensitivity, potentially offering a noninvasive, interpretable tool for pretreatment stratification.

paper.title: Deep Learning With Longitudinal Electrocardiograms Predicts Atrial Fibrillation Better Than a Single Electrocardiogram.
paper.abstract:
Background: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is often paroxysmal and asymptomatic, yet early identification could enable targeted surveillance. Deep learning can predict future AF from a single 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG), but AF develops through progressive atrial remodeling.
Objectives: We hypothesized that modeling each patient's longitudinal ECG history would improve 1-year AF prediction over a matched single-ECG model.
Methods: We developed a transformer-based model that accepts variable-length sequences of prior 12-lead ECGs with time-aware encoding of irregular intervals. We compared it with a single-ECG model sharing the same encoder, covariates, preprocessing, outcome definition, and splits. Models were developed at Weill Cornell Medicine/NewYork-Presbyterian and evaluated on MIMIC-IV-ECG without and with fine-tuning. The outcome was AF documented more than 1 and within 365 days after an index ECG. Discrimination used patient-cluster bootstrapping with 1 random index ECG per patient.
Results: Cohorts included 107,811 institutional and 55,307 MIMIC-IV-ECG patients. The fine-tuned longitudinal model with age and sex discriminated best (area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve: 0.85; C-index 0.84), exceeding the single-ECG model with age and sex (paired area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve: +0.007; 95% CI: 0.003-0.012; +0.014 with ≥1 prior ECG). Without retraining on MIMIC-IV-ECG, the ECG-only advantage was confined to patients with ≥1 prior ECG (+0.014; 95% CI: 0.004-0.024). After external-domain adaptation, the matched advantage was +0.007 (95% CI: 0.002-0.012). High-risk patients had lower AF-free survival (HR: 8.8; 95% CI: 7.8-10.0).
Conclusions: A longitudinal deep learning model using serial 12-lead ECGs improved 1-year AF prediction over a matched single-ECG model. Longitudinal ECG modeling may provide a scalable approach to identify patients warranting enhanced AF surveillance.

paper.title: Forecasting endodontic outcomes from intraoral radiographs using a deep convolutional neural network.
paper.abstract: This study aimed to develop and evaluate a generalized deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) model, ApexNet-17, for predicting endodontic outcomes across all tooth types using preoperative periapical radiographs. A dataset comprising 2,603 teeth from two institutions was utilized. Endodontic outcomes were determined based on tooth survival and radiographic periapical health during 1-3 years of follow-up using the periapical index (PAI). A 17-layer DCNN incorporating self-attention, attention pooling, and five radiographic features was trained and internally validated using 2,279 cases and externally tested using 324 cases. Gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) was applied to visualize regions contributing to model predictions. ApexNet-17 achieved an accuracy of 72.1%, a sensitivity of 58.5%, and an AUC of 0.666-performance that, while improved over the pilot model, remains below the level typically considered acceptable for clinical decision support. Compared with the previous premolar-only model, ApexNet-17 showed statistically higher accuracy and sensitivity (p < 0.05) but substantially lower specificity (50.6% vs. 78.3%), indicating a higher false-positive rate. Because the models were evaluated using different datasets, these comparisons should be interpreted cautiously, and statistical significance should not be regarded as evidence of clinical superiority. Limitations include the exclusion of intermediate PAI scores (2 and 3), the number and characteristics of which could not be assessed retrospectively, and the uncertain performance of the model in clinically ambiguous cases. Further refinement and validation are required before clinical implementation, although the findings support the feasibility of AI-based prediction of endodontic outcomes using preoperative periapical radiographs.

paper.title: Carotid plaque detection in patients with type 2 diabetes: development, interpretability, and limited transportability of a clinical model.
paper.abstract:
Objective: To develop and evaluate a parsimonious model for detecting prevalent carotid plaque in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and to assess its interpretability, robustness, and transportability.
Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study enrolled 2,035 hospitalized patients with T2DM, randomly assigned 70:30 to training and test sets. Bidirectional stepwise regression screened 39 candidate variables; stability was assessed by bootstrap resampling (1,000 replicates) and penalized regression. Performance was compared with random forest and XGBoost, and TreeSHAP was used for interpretability. Interaction terms, a non-medication model, and high-sensitivity thresholds were evaluated. The model was applied to an independent cohort of 3,191 health-screening individuals, with updating assessed by split-half validation.
Results: Eight predictors were retained. The test-set AUC was 0.827 (95% CI 0.791-0.862), versus 0.804 for random forest and 0.816 for XGBoost (P = 0.023 versus random forest). Only age and statin use were selected in 100% of bootstrap resamples. Removing statin use and GLP-1RA lowered the AUC to 0.787 (ΔAUC - 0.040, P < 0.001), retaining a history of coronary heart disease. No interaction term was significant (joint P = 0.511). In the external cohort, the AUC was 0.666 with marked miscalibration; updating left discrimination unchanged, and at 85% sensitivity, specificity was 33.4%.
Conclusion: An eight-variable logistic model using routinely available variables performed comparably to machine learning models for detecting prevalent carotid plaque in the development cohort. However, variable selection was unstable, and statin use was the strongest but indication-confounded correlate. External discrimination was moderate and did not improve after recalibration, indicating limited transportability. The model is best regarded as an exploratory candidate requiring further setting-specific validation, rather than one that may already aid in the detection of clinical cases.

paper.title: Opportunistic Risk Assessment of Major Osteoporotic Fractures from Routine Chest Radiographs Using Deep Learning.
paper.abstract:
Background: Bone mineral density (BMD) and the Fracture Risk Assessment Tool (FRAX) incompletely capture fracture risk in the osteopenic range, where much of the fracture burden occurs. Routine chest radiographs are acquired across a broad range of patients and may contain information relevant to fracture risk, offering a potential opportunistic complement without additional imaging burden.
Methods: We developed a convolutional neural network survival model in 53,109 adults at a tertiary hospital and externally validated it in 85,284 patients from two independent institutions. Eligibility required a chest radiograph obtained within 1 year of dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry scans, so all participants had been referred for densitometry. The primary outcome was incident major osteoporotic fracture. Discrimination was assessed by using the concordance index (C-index) and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) at 2, 3, 5, and 10 years, compared with FRAX with BMD and with the lowest BMD T-score.
Results: In the external validation cohorts (mean 58.6 years of age; 68.9% female; and follow-up of 77 months), the deep-learning (DL) model achieved a C-index of 0.843 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.837 to 0.850) and a censoring-adjusted 10-year AUROC of 0.855 (95% CI, 0.846 to 0.863), which was higher than that of FRAX with BMD (C-index, 0.779, 95% CI, 0.770 to 0.787; 10-year AUROC, 0.785, 95% CI, 0.775 to 0.794; both P<0.01). Adding FRAX to the DL model did not meaningfully improve discrimination (C-index, 0.847, 95% CI, 0.841 to 0.853). In the osteopenia subgroup (n=35,358), the DL model achieved a 10-year AUROC of 0.779 (95% CI, 0.764 to 0.795) versus 0.659 (95% CI, 0.641 to 0.676) for FRAX with BMD (P<0.01). This advantage was consistent across fracture types and BMD categories.
Conclusions: A survival DL model applied to routine chest radiographs identified patients at high fracture risk with discrimination exceeding that of FRAX, with the greatest benefit in patients with osteopenia. As all participants had been referred for densitometry, absolute-risk and case-finding estimates require prospective evaluation in an unselected routine-radiography population. (Funded by the National Research Foundation of Korea and others.).

paper.title: Development and External Validation of a Machine Learning-Based Predictive Model for Postoperative Recurrence in Pediatric Chronic Rhinosinusitis.
paper.abstract:
Background: Pediatric chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) frequently recurs after endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS), but reliable preoperative predictors are lacking, and adult-derived models may not apply to children. We developed and externally validated machine learning (ML) models to predict postoperative recurrence in pediatric CRS and identified key prognostic factors.
Methods: In this retrospective multicenter study, ML models-logistic regression (LR), random forest, XGBoost, and a stacking ensemble-were trained with class weighting on a development cohort of 633 pediatric ESS patients (aged 0-18 years), and an L1-optimized LR model was developed for variable selection from 33 candidate predictors. Performance was estimated by fivefold cross-validation, and the model was externally validated in 152 independent patients. Calibration was assessed using the Brier score, intercept, slope, and Hosmer-Lemeshow test, with logistic recalibration.
Results: Recurrence occurred in 242 of 633 patients (38.2%) in the development cohort and 46 of 152 patients (30.3%) in the external validation cohort. The L1-optimized LR model retained three predictors-nasal polyps, a higher Lund-Mackay CT score, and diffuse extent-each associated with higher recurrence risk, and achieved an AUC of 0.689, comparable to that of the other four class-weighted models. Laboratory findings and clinical symptoms were less predictive. On external validation, the model maintained discrimination (AUC = 0.756) but showed systematic miscalibration. Logistic recalibration restored calibration with essentially unchanged discrimination.
Conclusions: The three-variable L1-optimized LR model provides a concise framework for preoperative recurrence risk stratification in pediatric CRS that could inform postoperative surveillance. A site-specific recalibration step is required before application to populations with different recurrence rates.
